summary: Fresno State returns from its bye to host Oregon State at 8 p.m. PT Saturday. Pass protection and a steady rushing answer remain priorities after San Diego State; the Beavers bring a productive passing game.

items.headline: Oregon State visits Fresno at 8 p.m. PT on USA Sports
items.tldr: Both teams return from open dates for Saturday’s Halloween game. Plan for the late Pacific viewing window at Valley Children’s Stadium.

items.headline: Six sacks at San Diego State set the protection task
items.tldr: The October 17 loss ended with the final possession under pressure. Watch the quick outlet and pass sets after the bye rather than assuming the break resolved them.

items.headline: Donelson’s 62 rushing yards supplied an offensive answer
items.tldr: The Collegian’s review of the San Diego State game highlights his 13 carries and touchdown. Keep a useful first carry available when the passing pocket becomes crowded.

items.headline: Fresno State turns all three red-zone trips into touchdowns
items.tldr: The postgame notes identify the finishing work against San Diego State. The next offense needs enough sustained drives to make that execution matter again.

items.headline: Oregon State brings a long run of 300-yard passing games
items.tldr: The Beavers’ preview says Atkinson has passed for more than 300 yards in seven consecutive games. Watch receiver leverage and tackling before relying on pressure alone.

lead.headline: Give the next drive a clean answer.
lead.body: Keep a quick receiving outlet available when protection tightens. Pair it with a useful first carry, while the defense carries deeper routes and closes on the catch under control.

matchup.thesis: Make the protection and outlet arrive together
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: Choose routes the quarterback can reach before the pocket changes shape. On defense, keep the safety’s help connected to the receiver and make each completion finish through a tackle.

signals.title: Pass protection
signals.detail: Watch the tackle’s pass set and the nearest receiving outlet together. Do not ask the quarterback to wait through another hitch without a clean throwing lane.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with pass protection?

signals.title: Rushing continuity
signals.detail: Follow the first block and the runner’s decision through the crease. A useful ordinary gain can keep the passing game out of an obvious pressure down.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with rushing continuity?

signals.title: Red-zone execution
signals.detail: Get the first option into space near the goal line. Preserve the possession so a stalled opening read does not erase the work that reached scoring range.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with red-zone execution?

signals.title: Downfield defense
signals.summary: Carry the route through the catch
signals.detail: Keep leverage on the receiver while the safety tracks the deeper throw. Close under control and make the first tackle before the pursuit loses its shape.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with downfield defense?

nextGameNote: Watch the first pass-protection series and the first defensive tackle in space. Those ordinary plays will show whether the open week improved the next possession.
